gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a balcony solar generator built on the BLUETTI AC180 has to have its two 200 W panels wired in series, because the AC180 accepts at most 10 A and at most 60 V open-circuit and the SP200L is rated 24.6 V Voc and 10.8 A Isc, and that it needs an MC4 extension cable so the battery can stay indoors, since it charges only between 0 and 40 °C.
standout_why: I read the two pages ChatGPT cited (solar.com's 2026 balcony solar guide and pluginsolartracker.com's California page) and UL's UL 3700 announcement. None of them names a product or gives a panel voltage or current limit, a wiring rule, a temperature limit or a cable length. solar.com gives only price ranges by size and names microinverter makers (Hoymiles, APsystems, Mango Power). The tracker gives only SB 868 rules (1,200 W per dwelling, through a receptacle). UL gives no specs. ChatGPT's own answer showed two kits, the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic with a 160 W panel ($669) and the Anker C300 with a 60 W panel ($399.99), and said nothing about how to connect them. This finding decides which bundle to buy, how to wire it, and the extra cable that goes in the cart.
kit_items: Battery and inverter: BLUETTI AC180 (1,152 Wh LiFePO4, 1,800 W AC, 500 W solar input). It sits indoors and runs appliances from its own outlets, so it never sends power to the home's wiring. That keeps it outside the plug-in rules in SB 868 and UL 3700.

Panel: BLUETTI 200 W foldable (SP200L, 24.6 V Voc, 10.8 A Isc, IP67, MC4, 23.9 × 82.8 in unfolded). Two of them in series give 49.2 V, under the AC180's 60 V limit, and stay within its 10 A input. Wired in parallel they would put up to 21.6 A short-circuit current against that 10 A cap.
Cable: BLUETTI Solar Extension Cable, 5 m MC4 (30 A). It runs from the railing through the door to the indoor station, which charges only between 0 and 40 °C (32 to 104 °F).

Optional instead: BLUETTI 'AC180 + 2×200W Solar' bundle ($1,232), wired in series only. Never put a third 200 W panel in series: that is 73.8 V, which the manual says damages the unit and is not covered by warranty.

findings.label: Open-circuit voltage / short-circuit current
findings.note: Arithmetic: 2 in series = 49.2 V Voc (under 60 V), with current unchanged at 10.8 A Isc, so the AC180's 10 A limit trims it only slightly. 2 in parallel = 21.6 A Isc against the 10 A cap. 3 in series = 73.8 V, over the 60 V limit.

findings.value: 1,200 W max AC output per dwelling through a receptacle; effective 2027-01-01; certified whole-system protection against feeding the grid in an outage required

findings.note: Applies to grid-tied plug-in kits. A battery station that only runs appliances from its own outlets does not plug into the home's wiring.
